items.title: The Five Sciences Named, and Inner Wisdom's Fourfold Approach

items.zh: 何等名五明處？謂內明處、醫方明處、因明處、聲明處、工業明處。云何內明處？當知略說由四種相。一、由事施設建立相，二、由想差別施設建立相，三、由攝聖教義相，四、由佛教所應知處相。
items.en: What are called the five sciences? Namely: the science of inner wisdom, the science of medicine, the science of logic, the science of linguistics, and the science of the practical arts. What is the science of inner wisdom? Know that, briefly stated, it has four aspects: first, the aspect of establishing it by the designation of factual matters; second, the aspect of establishing it by the differentiation of conceptions; third, the aspect of that which comprises the meaning of the sacred teaching; fourth, the aspect of what a Buddhist ought to know.

items.title: The First Aspect: Scripture, Discipline, and Commentary — the Three Divisions Containing All of the Buddha's Teaching

items.zh: 云何事施設建立相？謂三種事，總攝一切諸佛言教。一、素怛纜事，二、毘奈耶事，三、摩怛履迦事。如是三事，攝事分中當廣分別。
items.en: What is the aspect of establishing it by the designation of factual matters? It is that three kinds of matters comprehend the entirety of all the Buddhas' verbal teaching. First, the matter of the sūtras; second, the matter of the vinaya; third, the matter of the mātṛkā. These three matters will be broadly differentiated in the Compendium of Topics.

items.zh: 云何想差別施設建立相？
items.en: What is the characteristic of the establishment of differences in perception?

items.title: The Second Aspect Opens: A Verse of Twelve Terms, and "Word" Illustrated Through the Śrāvakayāna's Thirteen Categories

items.zh: 嗢拕南曰：句、迷惑、戲論、住、真實、淨、妙、寂靜、性、道理、假施設、現觀。云何句？謂內六處無量境界、無量方所、無量時分。復有三界。謂欲界、色界、無色界。又有三界。謂小千世界、中千世界、三千大千世界。復有四眾。謂在家眾、出家眾、鄔波索迦眾、非人眾。復有三受。謂苦受、樂受、不苦不樂受。復有三世。謂過去世、未來世、現在世。復有三寶。謂佛寶、法寶、僧寶。復有三法。謂善法、不善法、無記法。復有三雜染。謂煩惱雜染、業雜染、生雜染。復有四聖諦。謂苦聖諦、集聖諦、滅聖諦、道聖諦。復有九次第等至。謂初靜慮等至，乃至滅想受等至。復有三十七菩提分法。謂四念住、四正斷、四神足、五根、五力、七覺支、八道支。復有四沙門果。謂預流果、一來果、不還果、最勝阿羅漢果。復有眾多勝妙功德。謂無量、解脫、勝處、遍處、無諍、願智、無礙解、六神通等。
items.en: The summarising verse: "Word, delusion, discursive proliferation; abiding, reality, purity, excellence; tranquility, nature, principle; provisional designation, direct realisation." What is "word"? The six inner sense-bases have boundless objects, boundless locations, and boundless spans of time. There are also the three realms: desire, form, and formless. And there are [another] three realms: the small chiliocosm, the medium chiliocosm, and the great trichiliocosm. There are the four assemblies: householders, renunciants, lay devotees, and non-humans. There are the three feelings: painful, pleasant, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant. There are the three times: past, future, and present. There are the three jewels: the Buddha-jewel, the Dharma-jewel, and the Saṅgha-jewel. There are the three dharmas: wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. There are the three defilements: afflictive, karmic, and rebirth defilement. There are the four noble truths: suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. There are the nine successive attainments: the first-dhyāna attainment up through the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling. There are the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment: the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of supernormal power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path. There are the four fruits of the ascetic path: stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and the most excellent fruit of arhatship. And there are many sublime qualities: the immeasurables, the liberations, the [eight] bases of mastery, the [ten] totalities, [the concentration of] non-contention, wish-fulfilling knowledge, unobstructed understanding, and the six superknowledges, and so forth.

items.title: "Word" Continues: The Mahāyāna's Five Bases, Two Emptinesses, and Two Selflessnesses

items.zh: 復有方廣大乘五事。謂相、名、分別、真如、正智。復有二空性。謂補特伽羅空性、及法空性。復有二無我性。謂補特伽羅無我性，及法無我性。
items.en: There are also, in the extensive Mahāyāna teaching, the five bases: characteristic-mark, name, discrimination, suchness, and correct wisdom. There are also two emptinesses: the emptiness of a person, and the emptiness of phenomena. There are also two selflessnesses: the selflessness of a person, and the selflessness of phenomena.

items.title: Avoiding Two Extremes, and Four Grades of Reality

items.zh: 復有遠離二邊處中觀行。謂離增益邊、離損減邊。復有四種真實。謂世間所成真實、道理所成真實、煩惱障淨智所行真實、所知障淨智所行真實。
items.en: There is also the middle-way contemplation that abandons two extremes: abandoning the extreme of superimposition, and abandoning the extreme of denial. There are also four kinds of reality: reality established by worldly convention, reality established by reasoning, reality that is the domain of the wisdom purified of afflictive obstruction, and reality that is the domain of the wisdom purified of the obstruction to what can be known.

items.title: The Four Investigations and Four Kinds of True Knowledge — the Working Method of Yogācāra Practice

items.zh: 復有四尋思。謂名尋思、事尋思、自性假立尋思、差別假立尋思。復有四如實遍智。謂名尋思所引如實遍智、事尋思所引如實遍智、自性假立尋思所引如實遍智、差別假立尋思所引如實遍智。
items.en: There are also the four investigations: investigation into names, investigation into things, investigation into the provisional positing of intrinsic nature, and investigation into the provisional positing of differentiation. There are also the four kinds of thorough true knowledge: the thorough true knowledge induced by investigation into names, the thorough true knowledge induced by investigation into things, the thorough true knowledge induced by investigation into the provisional positing of intrinsic nature, and the thorough true knowledge induced by investigation into the provisional positing of differentiation.

items.title: The Three Natures and Three Kinds of Non-Nature — Yogācāra's Central Teaching

items.zh: 復有三種自性。謂遍計所執自性、依他起自性、圓成實自性。復有三無性性。謂相無性性、生無性性、勝義無性性。
items.en: There are also three intrinsic natures: the nature of thorough imagination and attachment, the nature of dependent arising, and the nature of perfect and complete accomplishment. There are also three kinds of the nature of having no [intrinsic] nature: the nature of having no nature with respect to characteristic-marks, the nature of having no nature with respect to arising, and the nature of having no nature in the ultimate sense.

items.title: The Five Aspects of Great Enlightenment, the Five Facets of the Mahāyāna, and Five Kinds of Boundless Conception

items.zh: 復有五相大菩提。謂自性故、功能故、方便故、轉故、還故。復有五種大乘。一、種子，二、趣入，三、次第，四、正行，五、正行果。最初發心，悲愍有情，波羅蜜多，攝眾生事，自他相續成熟。復有五無量想。謂有情界無量想、世界無量想、法界無量想、所調伏界無量想、調伏方便界無量想。
items.en: There are also five aspects of great enlightenment: by way of intrinsic nature, by way of capability, by way of skilful means, by way of activity, and by way of return. There are also five facets of the Mahāyāna: first, the seed; second, entry; third, sequence; fourth, correct practice; fifth, the fruit of correct practice. There are also five kinds of boundless conception: boundless conception with respect to the realm of sentient beings, boundless conception with respect to the world, boundless conception with respect to the realm of phenomena, boundless conception with respect to the realm to be tamed, and boundless conception with respect to the realm of skilful means for taming.

items.title: The Seven Kinds of Suchness, and a Buddha's Inconceivable Qualities — "Word" Concludes

items.zh: 復有真實義隨至。謂於一切無量法中遍隨至真如及於彼智。復有不思議威德勝解、無障礙智、三十二大士夫相、八十種隨形相、四種一切相清淨、十力、四無所畏、三念住、三不護、大悲、無忘失法、拔除習氣、一切相妙智等。如是諸句，略唯二句。謂聲聞乘中所說句，及大乘中所說句。
items.en: There is also the true meaning that pervasively attends [all phenomena]: namely, suchness, which pervasively attends throughout all boundless phenomena, together with the wisdom [that knows] it. There are also a buddha's inconceivable might and resolve, unobstructed wisdom, the thirty-two marks of a great being, the eighty subsidiary marks, the four kinds of universal purity, the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three foundations of mindfulness, the three things requiring no guarding, great compassion, the dharma of never forgetting, the eradication of habitual residue, and the sublime wisdom of every kind, and so forth. All such words are, in brief, of only two kinds: those spoken of within the Śrāvakayāna, and those spoken of within the Mahāyāna.

items.title: Delusion, Discursive Proliferation, the Stations of Consciousness, and Reality

items.zh: 云何迷惑？謂四顛倒。一、於無常計常顛倒，二、於苦計樂顛倒，三、於不淨計淨顛倒，四、於無我計我顛倒。云何戲論？謂一切煩惱，及雜煩惱諸蘊。云何住？謂四識住，或七識住。云何真實？謂真如及四聖諦。
items.en: What is delusion? The four inversions. What is discursive proliferation? All afflictions, and the aggregates entangled with affliction. What is abiding? The four stations of consciousness, or the seven stations of consciousness. What is reality? Suchness, and the four noble truths.

blocks.text: The tenth stage, the **Stage Attained Through Hearing** (聞所成地), begins the second group of stages (10–15), which describe **practice** (Introduction 2). Hearing comes first: the treatise lists what a practitioner should learn. Its first subject, "inner wisdom", is a compressed glossary of Yogācāra's core teachings. Several of them, the five bases, the four investigations, the three natures, are Yogācāra's distinctive contribution, and you will recognise them from Introduction 1.

The stage is defined as "listening to, receiving, reciting, and remembering", with innate discernment leading, the names, phrases, and letters of the **five sciences** (五明處): **inner wisdom** (內明, Buddhist teaching), **medicine**, **logic**, **linguistics**, and the **practical arts**. A bodhisattva learns all five, because each can serve beings.

Inner wisdom is presented in four aspects. Master Cháng Bǎi: the third comprehends the teaching through ten principles; the fourth reveals principle through the teaching. The first is the three divisions of scripture: sūtra, vinaya, and *mātṛkā* (Master Cháng Bǎi: "the mother", the mother of wisdom, also called treatise). Ru-Yi's English reads one reference as the *Compendium of Ascertainments*; both teachers read it as the *Compendium of Topics* (攝事分).

The second aspect is explained through a verse of key terms. The first is "word": the categories a śrāvaka must know, from the four assemblies to the Three Jewels. Venerable Miào Jìng: the verbal teaching is the "expedient" Dharma-jewel; "the true Dharma-jewel is nirvāṇa."

items: **Five bases** (五事): characteristic-mark, name, discrimination, suchness, and correct wisdom.
**Two emptinesses and two selflessnesses**: of persons and of phenomena.
**Four grades of reality**: what the world agrees on, what reasoning establishes, what purifies from afflictive obscuration, and what purifies from cognitive obscuration.

**Four investigations and four true knowledges** (四尋思、四如實智): investigating name, thing, self-nature, and differentiation, and then knowing each as it truly is. Master Cháng Bǎi: the investigations are practised at the "heat" and "summit" stages of preparation; the true knowledges at "forbearance" and "supreme mundane". This is the working method of Yogācāra insight.

**Three natures and three non-natures** (三自性、三無性), the school's central teaching (Introduction 1). Venerable Miào Jìng: the perfected nature "is complete, originally so, indestructible, with real substance"; here he sees a difference in emphasis from Madhyamaka.
**Five aspects of great enlightenment**, five facets of the Mahāyāna (seed, entry, sequence, correct practice, fruit), and **seven kinds of suchness**.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi on one of a Buddha's qualities, "eradicating habitual residue": Maudgalyāyana, a monkey for five hundred lives, still felt the urge to jump on hearing music. An arhat cuts afflictions; only a Buddha removes even their residue.

Delusion is the four inversions; proliferation is all afflictions and the afflicted aggregates. Venerable Miào Jìng's plain definition of proliferation: "wasting a great deal of energy and time and getting nothing at all from it."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the Ground of What Is Attained Through Hearing?
options: with innate discernment leading, listening to, receiving, reciting, and remembering the five sciences' names, phrases, and letters, and understanding their meaning without inversion
quiz.why: "With respect to the boundless distinctions among the name-bodies, phrase-bodies, and letter-bodies of the five sciences, with innate discernment leading the way, the activities of listening, receiving, reciting, and remembering … one comes to understand them without inversion." Venerable Miào Jìng: this discernment is innate wisdom.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the five sciences?
options: inner wisdom, medicine, logic, linguistics, practical arts
quiz.why: "The science of inner wisdom, the science of medicine, the science of logic, the science of linguistics, and the science of the practical arts." Venerable Miào Jìng: inner wisdom is, roughly, the Buddhadharma — what matters most for us.

quiz.q: The text says the three matters "will be broadly differentiated in the 攝事分." The translation renders it "Compendium of Determinations." Is that right?
options: no — 攝事分 is the Compendium of Topics; "Determinations" is the 攝決擇分
quiz.why: The text says 攝事分, as both teachers read; the translation mistakes it for the Compendium of Determinations (logged). Venerable Miào Jìng: mātṛkā, the "mother," has principle as its root and gives birth to wisdom.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the Mahāyāna's five bases?
options: characteristic-mark, name, discrimination, suchness, correct wisdom
quiz.why: "There are also, in the extensive Mahāyāna teaching, the five bases: characteristic-mark, name, discrimination, suchness, and correct wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: in fundamental non-discriminating wisdom, all of these vanish — supramundane correct wisdom.

quiz.q: At which of the four preparatory stages are the four investigations and four true knowledges, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the investigations are at heat and summit; the true knowledges at forbearance and the supreme mundane stage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The four investigations are practised at the heat and summit stages"; "at forbearance and supreme mundane, bodhisattvas truly know name unobtainable, thing unobtainable." The reading note's placing of the true knowledges at heat and summit is wrong (logged).

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the three natures?
options: the imagined, the dependent, and the perfected
quiz.why: "There are also three intrinsic natures: the nature of thorough imagination and attachment, the nature of dependent arising, and the nature of perfect and complete accomplishment." Venerable Miào Jìng: the imagined is what ordinary beings cling to though it doesn't exist — the snake on the rope.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng say the perfected nature differs from the Madhyamaka?
options: it is complete, originally so, indestructible, with real substance — unlike the Madhyamaka
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "It is complete, originally so — hence 'accomplished' — indestructible, with real substance. This is where it differs from the *Madhyamaka*." Without the self-nature of proliferation it is "natureless," yet that naturelessness has substance.
